html:
King of the Achaemenid Persian Empire from 522 to 486 BCE, who gave the vast realm won by Cyrus the Great and his son Cambyses its lasting shape.

He took the throne in a palace coup and spent his first year crushing revolts across the empire, a story he carved on the cliff of the Behistun Inscription. Then he organised. He divided the empire into provinces called satrapies, each with a governor and fixed tribute. He issued a gold coin, the daric, built the Royal Road with its relay posts, and finished a canal linking the Nile to the Red Sea. He began the palace city of Persepolis.

He pushed the empire to its greatest size, adding the Indus Valley and Thrace. When the Greek cities of Ionia rose in the Ionian Revolt with help from Athens, he crushed them and sent a fleet to punish Athens, which lost at the Battle of Marathon in 490 BCE. He died while planning a larger war, which his son Xerxes I carried out.
sum: King of the Achaemenid Persian Empire from 522 to 486 BCE, who gave the vast realm won by Cyrus the Great and his son Cambyses its lasting shape.
